modules.intro: You present your trophy: five parts, five machines, and what your measurements showed about each one. Eight slides, five minutes, two questions. This module is the deck you present from. It is due before anyone presents, not on the day you present.
modules.title: Slide by slide
modules.aiNote: AI may suggest layouts and tighten sentences you wrote. It may not generate images, and every picture on the deck is a photo you took or a screenshot of your own work.

blocks.content:
Eight slides, 4:3, in this order. Put the station name on each of slides 2 through 6. That leaves about 35 seconds for pauses and moving between slides.

```
 1  TITLE      trophy photo       10s
 2  BASE       H2D Laser          30s
 3  COLUMN     Mill               30s
 4  PLATFORM   Axiom Router       30s
 5  SHAFT      Lathe              30s
 6  TOPPER     xTool MetalFab     30s
 7  NUMBERS    your measurements  45s
 8  FINDINGS   what it showed     60s
                        total   4:25
```

**Every station slide carries four things.**

1. A clear photo of the part you made.
2. A photo of the drawing you made for that part. On slide 6 this is a screenshot of your topper design in xTool Studio instead.
3. One line from your notebook naming something specific that happened at that machine: a problem, a mistake, a measurement, or something you changed. "It went fine" is not a line.
4. One process decision you made there.

**A process decision names what you chose and what you chose it over.** Which tool, what speed or feed, how you held it, what order you cut in, or a setting you changed from the default. "I used the mill" is not a decision.

**What each slide is for**

**Slide 1, Title, 10 sec.** Your name and a photo of the assembled trophy. You say your name and hold up the trophy. Nothing else.

**Slides 2 to 6, 30 sec each.** Say the station, the decision you made there, and what happened because of it. Thirty seconds is about three sentences, so do not narrate the whole process. The images carry the rest.

items: Eight slides, 4:3, in the order shown
Each station slide is labeled with its station name
Each station slide has a photo of the part I made
Each station slide has my drawing, or my xTool design on slide 6
Each station slide has a line from my notebook about what happened
Each station slide names one process decision

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Deck is 4:3, all eight slides are in order, and every station slide carries the part photo, the drawing (or the xTool screenshot on slide 6), a notebook line naming something specific, and a process decision.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: All eight slides present, with one required element missing from one station slide, or the deck is not 4:3.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Six or seven slides, or a required element missing from two or more station slides.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Fewer than six slides, or no deck submitted.

modules.intro: The images do most of the work in this deck. These are the rules for them.
modules.title: Your images
modules.aiNote: AI may suggest layouts and tighten sentences you wrote. It may not generate images, and every picture on the deck is a photo you took or a screenshot of your own work.

blocks.content:
**Every image on this deck is a photo you took or a screenshot of your own work. No AI-generated images. No stock photos off the internet.**

An AI picture of a lathe is not a picture of your lathe, and it will not survive a question.

**Good visual aids**

- Your finished part on a clean bench, whole part in frame, in focus.
- Your paper drawing, photographed flat, straight on, readable.
- A screenshot of your toolpath in Aspire, or your laser job in xTool Studio or Bambu Suite.
- A photo of the machine mid-cut, or your setup in the vise or chuck.
- Your measurement table, or a bar chart of your differences.

**Not acceptable**

- An AI-generated image of anything.
- A stock photo of a machine you did not use.
- The CAD model in place of a photo of your actual part.
- A blurry photo, a photo at an angle where the part is hard to see, or a part buried in chips.

**A photo counts if someone who was not there can tell what they are looking at.** Take it in good light, get the whole part in the frame, and look at it before you use it. If a part broke, photograph what you have.

**Word and image limits**

**The title slide has no word limit.** Every other slide has a limit of 35 words. Slide titles count. Text inside a table counts. The only exemption is the numeric values in your slide 7 data table.

Every slide except the title carries an image filling at least a third of it.

items: Every image is a photo I took or a screenshot of my own work
No AI-generated images anywhere in the deck
Every part photo is in focus with the whole part in frame
My drawing photos are readable, flat and straight on
No slide except the title has more than 35 words
Every slide except the title has an image filling at least a third of it

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Every image is the student's own photo or screenshot, every part is identifiable in its photo, no slide except the title exceeds 35 words, and every slide except the title carries an image filling at least a third of it.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: One image is unusable, generated, or sourced elsewhere, or one slide exceeds 35 words, or one slide is missing its image.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Two or three images or slides fail on those grounds.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Four or more images or slides fail on those grounds, or the deck relies on generated or stock images.

modules.intro: Slides 7 and 8 carry your own data. Write the conclusion here before you put it on a slide, then hand in the link.
modules.title: Your numbers and your conclusion
modules.aiNote: AI may tighten sentences you wrote. It may not decide which process held closest, choose your reason, or write the conclusion for you.

blocks.content:
**Slide 7, Numbers, 45 sec.** Your table: nominal, measured, and difference for all five parts. Difference is measured minus nominal; keep the minus sign.

Do not read the table out loud. Point at it and say three things: the biggest difference you measured and which part it was on, the part that came out closest, and how many of your five parts came out over nominal and how many came out under.

**Slide 8, Findings, 60 sec.** This is the slide that matters most. Four beats, about 15 seconds each.

1. **Closest and furthest.** Name the process that held its dimensions closest to nominal and the one that was furthest off. Compare the single largest difference on each part, and **ignore the minus sign when you compare.** A part off by 0.020 under is further off than one 0.010 over.
2. **The reason.** Pick one of four: the size of the tool or the beam, how the material behaves, how the part was held, or how the machine moves.
3. **The proof.** Tie that reason to one number from your own table. Say the number out loud.
4. **The ranking.** List all five processes in order, closest to furthest.

If you get stuck, say the number first and the reason second. The number is yours and nobody can argue with it.

Build the deck in Google Slides, PowerPoint, or Canva. **Turn view access on, then open your own link in a private window. If the link does not open, the whole deck scores zero, all ten points.** Test it before you paste it.

columns.tip: View access on for anyone with the link. Test it in a private window before you paste it.
columns.label: Link to your deck

blocks.prompt: Write your slide 8 conclusion here before you put it on the slide. Name the process that held its dimensions closest to nominal, the process that was furthest off, one reason for the gap from these four (tool or beam size, how the material behaves, how the part was held, how the machine moves), and one number from your own table that supports it.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Slide 7 shows nominal, measured and signed difference for all five parts, and the conclusion names both processes, a reason from the four, and one of their own numbers.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Slide 7 is complete and the conclusion names both processes and a reason, without citing a measured number.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Slide 7 is missing values or parts, or the conclusion names one process only, or gives no reason from the four.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No conclusion written or no measurement data. A link that does not open scores zero here and on the other two deck criteria.

modules.intro: You walk the class through your trophy and what you found making it. Slides are on the screen. Your five parts are on the bench in front of you.
modules.title: Present your portfolio

blocks.content:
Seven minutes each. Five minutes presenting, two minutes of questions. At five minutes you stop, wherever you are.

How the days work:

- **Block 3:** presentations run across two class days, half the class each day. The order is posted before the first day.
- **Blocks 2 and 4:** every presentation happens in one class day.

Your deck is due before the first presentation day in every section. If you present on the second day, the deadline was still the first day.

What you cover in five minutes:

- The process decision you made at each of the five stations.
- Which process held its dimensions closest to nominal and which was furthest off. **Compare the single largest difference on each part, ignoring the minus sign.**
- Why. Name one of these four: the size of the tool or the beam, how the material behaves, how the part was held, or how the machine moves. Then tie it to one of your own numbers.

The two minutes of questions:

You will be asked **exactly two questions.** If the class does not ask two, the instructor asks the rest. They are about what you did and what you measured, not about whether your choices were right. Everyone made the same five parts.

Reading a slide out loud is not an answer. If you do not know, say so and say what you would measure to find out.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: States a process decision at all five stations, each naming a tool, setting, workholding, or sequence choice and what it was chosen over. Naming the machine or the operation alone does not count.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: States a qualifying choice at all five stations without naming what it was chosen over, or names choice and alternative at four.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: States a qualifying decision at two or three stations.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: States a qualifying decision at one station or none.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names the closest and furthest process using their own largest differences, gives a reason from the four listed, ties that reason to one of their measured numbers, and ranks all five processes closest to furthest.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Names both processes from their own numbers and gives a reason from the four listed, but either does not tie it to a measured value or does not rank all five.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Reads measurements aloud without naming which process was closest and furthest, or names them with no reason from the four.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Does not refer to their own measurements.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Answers both questions with a specific detail of their own setup, tooling, or measurement that is not written on a slide.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Answers one question from their own work and answers the other by repeating slide content.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Answers both questions by repeating slide content, or answers one and cannot answer the other.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Answers neither question, or does not present.
